rationale: Both implement the subclassing and delegation wrappers cleanly with the same counters and properties. B is simpler and more coherent. It meters readline() itself and has __next__ delegate to it, so a direct readline call and iteration are both counted, through a single code path. A counts only inside __next__, so a direct readline() call goes unmetered. A also adds machinery that is not needed: a _REQUIRED sentinel to re-implement the missing-argument TypeError that Python already raises, and a _check_flags type check that duplicates what the underlying socket does. A's guard in __getattr__ against recursion on private names is a genuine robustness touch that B lacks. Overall, B's leaner design and more complete read metering make it the better solution.
